channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: US returns to Africa with investment-first strategy as competition for influence intensifies
item.description: The United States is recalibrating its Africa engagement around an investment-first strategy as competition for economic and geopolitical influence on the continent sharpens.

item.title: Russia helps ward off an attack on Niger close to French-linked nuclear materials
item.description: The Diori Hamani International Airport on the outskirts of Niamey, Niger’s capital, recently came under an attack by suspected terrorists.

item.title: After $3 billion takeover, Canal+ plans unified streaming service for MultiChoice users in South Africa
item.description: Canal+ SA, the French media group that recently acquired South African pay-TV operator MultiChoice in a deal valued at about $3 billion, is preparing to launch a unified streaming service across the region.

item.title: Tanzania to seal $42bn LNG deal as push to become East Africa's energy hub continues
item.description: Tanzania is pushing to conclude one of Africa’s most ambitious energy investments, renewing efforts to finalise a $42 billion liquefied natural gas agreement by mid 2026 as it seeks to position itself as East Africa’s emerging energy hub.

item.title: US begins $70 million military base expansion in Kenya to step up fight against Al-Shabaab
item.description: The United States has begun a $70 million expansion of a key military airstrip at Kenya’s Manda Bay base, deepening security cooperation between Washington and Nairobi as concerns over extremist violence persist across the Horn of Africa.

item.title: Ranking Africa’s top 10 defence spenders vs their military strength in 2026
item.description: Africa’s defence industry is at a pivotal moment as security threats intensify across the continent.

item.title: South Africa gives Israel envoy 72 hours to exit the country, emphasizes policy autonomy
item.description: South Africa has expelled an Israeli diplomat, Mr Ariel Seidman in a move that shows Pretoria’s willingness to pursue an independent foreign policy, even as it risks friction with key Western partners, including the United States.

item.title: Mozambique enters graphite processing with new Chinese-owned facility
item.description: Mozambique’s President Daniel Chapo inaugurated a 200,000 metric ton-per-year graphite processing plant at a Chinese-owned mine.

item.title: 10 African countries with the highest Chinese loans in the last 24 years
item.description: According to the Chinese Loans to Africa (CLA) Database, which is maintained by Boston University's Global Development Policy Center, Chinese loan pledges to African states will fall to just under $2.1 billion in 2024, spread across only six projects.

item.title: Investors race into Madagascar as 16-year mining ban is lifted, gold excluded
item.description: Madagascar has lifted a 16-year moratorium on issuing new mining permits for most minerals, reopening a sector central to Africa’s critical-minerals race and the island nation’s evolving geopolitical posture.
